### [1] McCabe, T. J. (1976). "A Complexity Measure."

- **URL**: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclomatic_complexity (secondary; original: IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, SE-2(4), 308-320, December 1976)
- **Tier**: 1 (peer-reviewed paper, accessed via secondary sources)
- **Data extracted**: Cyclomatic complexity definition, formula M = E - N + 2P, threshold of 10, risk categories, essential complexity, basis path testing relationship, compound predicate counting
- **Access note**: Original paper not directly fetched. Claims verified through multiple independent secondary sources (Wikipedia, Microsoft Learn, NIST SP 500-235 citations, JetBrains compilation). All secondary sources consistently reproduce the same formulas and threshold language.

### [2] Watson, A. H. & McCabe, T. J. (1996). "Structured Testing: A Testing Methodology Using the Cyclomatic Complexity Metric." NIST Special Publication 500-235.

- **URL**: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication500-235.pdf
- **Tier**: 1 (government/institutional report)
- **Data extracted**: Limit of 10 as "good starting point," limits up to 15 with operational advantages, structured testing methodology, test adequacy criterion ("a module should have at least as many tests as its cyclomatic complexity")
